clinicalPearls: A variant of herpetic (usually varicella-zoster) necrotising retinitis occurring in severely immunocompromised patients, classically advanced HIV
Distinguished from acute retinal necrosis by minimal or absent intraocular inflammation and by early posterior-pole and outer-retinal involvement
Multifocal deep retinal opacification spreads rapidly and coalesces, often with early macular involvement
Retinal vasculitis is typically absent, unlike acute retinal necrosis
Progression is extremely rapid and the prognosis for vision is poor
Management combines systemic and intravitreal antivirals with restoration of immune function
reference.pathophysiology: In the setting of profound cellular immunodeficiency, varicella-zoster virus infects the outer retina, producing rapidly progressive necrosis that begins in the deep retina and posterior pole with little inflammatory response because the immune system cannot mount vitritis or vasculitis. The outer-retinal predilection and blunted inflammation reflect the underlying immunosuppression, and confluent necrosis frequently reaches the macula early, causing severe irreversible visual loss and a high rate of retinal detachment.
additionalDifferentials: Acute retinal necrosis (immunocompetent, prominent vitritis and vasculitis)
additionalInvestigations: Vitreous or aqueous PCR for varicella-zoster and other herpesviruses
HIV testing and CD4 count / immune status assessment
Dilated fundus examination documenting outer-retinal necrosis
Syphilis and other infective serology to exclude mimics
Optical coherence tomography and wide-field imaging to track progression
redFlags: Rapidly advancing necrosis toward or involving the macula
Very low CD4 count or other severe immunosuppression
reference.prognosis: Prognosis is poor with frequent rapid progression to profound visual loss and retinal detachment; outcomes improve when immune reconstitution is achieved alongside antiviral therapy.
pitfalls: Expecting the vitritis of acute retinal necrosis and dismissing PORN because the eye looks quiet
Delaying antiviral therapy while awaiting confirmatory tests
Neglecting to address the underlying immunosuppression
management: Commence high-dose systemic antiviral therapy directed at varicella-zoster virus, typically intravenous aciclovir combined with ganciclovir or foscarnet, without waiting for PCR confirmation
Add repeated intravitreal ganciclovir or foscarnet injections to achieve therapeutic intraocular antiviral levels
Restore immune function by starting or optimising antiretroviral therapy in HIV, or reducing iatrogenic immunosuppression, as this is central to controlling the infection
Monitor progression with serial dilated fundoscopy, wide-field imaging and optical coherence tomography, watching for macular and peripheral spread
Refer urgently to vitreoretinal surgery for prophylactic laser demarcation and repair of the frequent rhegmatogenous retinal detachment
Manage jointly with infectious diseases and HIV physicians and continue oral valaciclovir maintenance to protect the fellow eye and prevent relapse
